Rishi / team / Aurium —

Thanks, Santiago — useful redline. High level: we should avoid absolute language about backups that implies we can modify immutable snapshot retention controlled by underlying cloud providers, but we can offer a practical, auditable commitment. Two candidate clauses below (option A = narrower, option B = customer-friendly compromise). Please pick one or tell me which parts to combine.

Option A (operationally conservative):
"Upon Customer's verified request for erasure, Redwood Inference will (i) remove Customer Data from active production storage within thirty (30) days, and (ii) commence a process to remove Customer Data from scope of backups and snapshots as soon as practicable, which may require up to sixty (60) days for certain provider-managed snapshot retention. Redwood will provide a certified erasure report (manifest) within ninety (90) days detailing the locations processed and the method applied; such report will include exception items and remediation plans if immediate removal was infeasible."

Option B (customer-centric compromise):
"Upon Customer's verified request for erasure, Redwood Inference will remove Customer Data from active production storage within fifteen (15) days and use commercially reasonable efforts to delete the data from backups, snapshots and replicas within forty-five (45) days. Redwood will provide a certified erasure manifest within sixty (60) days. For backups or provider-managed immutable snapshots that cannot be deleted, Redwood will (i) isolate such copies and (ii) ensure they are rendered inaccessible to Redwood personnel and agents until deletion is feasible, and will include these items in the manifest along with a target remediation date."

Key considerations for Aurium: Option B is friendlier but commits us to faster primary removal and shorter manifest turnaround; it relies on our operational isolation controls for immutable items. Option A gives us more buffer but adds additional reporting time.

I recommend Option B with a carveout for "onshore archival escrow" if Aurium requires certified onshore-only backups — that can be negotiated as a separately priced addendum.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick operational note from infra/ops:

- Primary data (hot stores, KV cache, model-processed artifacts) can be purged within 15 days end-to-end if we schedule an expedited erase and block writes.
- Cold backups and provider-managed immutable snapshots typically obey provider retention policies; for many clouds we can request early deletion but cannot force immediate purge; 30–45 days is realistic as per Laura's Option B.
- For cross-region replicas, we can chain the delete requests; propagation time depends on replication windows (usually within 24–72 hours for active replication, but eventual deletion follows the backup windows above).
- We can produce a certified manifest: a short PDF listing affected object IDs, regions, and the deletion method (API delete, tombstone + TTL, isolation flag) and a signed ops contact. We already do this for some enterprise customers.

Operational exception: where onshore-only archival or third-party escrow is involved (customer-managed), we cannot certify deletion of that copy without coordination with the escrow provider; recommend a one-paragraph carveout.

I’ll work with Soojin to map the exact steps and runbook entries into the manifest template.

Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Operations
